items.title: Igbo rebuff of today’s Nigerian Army (I), by Ochereome Nnanna
items.description: For some years now, youths of the Igbo ethnic group, especially in the five states of the South East geopolitical zone, have been shunning enrolment into the military. In 2025, a Brigadier General, Chima Ekeator, led a team round the geopolitical zone canvassing for Igbo youths to take up their quotas. For instance, he said Kaduna State indigenes, like youths of most other states, oversubscribed their state quota, while Enugu State failed to raise up to 100 recruits to fill its 200 slots. This year, the Brigadier General in charge of the Nigerian Army’s Ohafia Division, A. M. Dikko, lamented that he failed to fill his slot as only a few showed up for recruitment. The question is: why have Igbo youths lost interest in the same Army they once bestrode like the proverbial colossus? The answer is simple: no sense of belonging. Before Nigeria’s independence and the Biafra War, Igbo and Eastern youths dominated the officer corps of the Nigerian military and security services. The Igbo were at the forefront of the fight for Nigeria’s independence, and they looked forward, alongside their compatriots, to defending its sovereignty. For some of those graduating from colleges, the military offered a prestigious career opportunity. Pioneers like the billionaire’s son, Chukwuemeka Odumegwu Ojukwu (who joined the officer corps after obtaining a Master’s degree at Oxford), Okoh Ebitu Ukiwe, Godwin Ndubuisi Kanu, Allison Madueke, Alexander Madiebo, Obi Rapu and so many others joined the Army and Navy in the late 1950s. Madiebo, in his book, Nigerian Revolution and Biafra War, documents how, by 1963, Igbo officers dominated the Nigerian Army. Indeed, the very first full General and first military Head of State of Nigeria was an Igbo man – Johnson Thomas Aguiyi-Ironsi. For whatever it is worth, I need to recall that the first military coup was led by an Igbo man, Major Chukwuma Kaduna Nzeogwu, and Ironsi, as Head of State, led the forces to quell the coup. This says it all: Ndi Igbo once occupied the alpha position in the Armed Forces of the Federal Republic of Nigeria. Let me also note that the Igbo did not join the lower ranks with the same enthusiasm. This “other ranks” cadre was dominated mainly by Hausa and Northern elements, which were later mobilised to attack their Igbo officers when the first coup occasioned the killing of Northern political leaders. After the Biafra War, many Igbo youths desired to rejoin the Nigerian armed forces, more especially as Gen. Yakubu Gowon proclaimed his fraudulent “No Victor, No Vanquished”, giving the impression that the nation had put the war behind it. What actually happened was that the British-manipulated Federal Military Government sought to hoodwink the ex-Biafrans while the war was continued through hostile government policies. Many Igbo youths who struggled to join the Army, Police, Air Force and other uniformed forces were either stiff-armed or given a ceiling above which they would not be allowed to rise. They endured decades of marginalisation, early retirement and exclusion from occupying certain ranks and command positions. They kept struggling until just about a decade ago, when Muhammadu Buhari came back to power as an elected president. The only time, since the War, when an Igbo, Lt.-General Azubuike Ihejirika, was appointed Chief of Army Staff, was during the regime of President Goodluck Jonathan. Ihejirika was the last Nigerian Army Chief who fought Boko Haram terrorists like the Nigerian Army we all knew and respected. He was on the verge of defeating the jihadists when, suddenly, Northern politicians and Islamic clerics began accusing him and President Jonathan of “fighting the North” and “killing Northerners”. The Sultan of Sokoto, Nasir el-Rufai, Muhammadu Buhari and Borno elders were all on this chorus. Indeed, Amnesty International (AI), curiously, joined them, showing more concern for the dirty blows being administered on the terrorists than for the fate of Boko Haram victims in North East communities and refugee camps. President Jonathan, who was fervently seeking Northern support for his second term, panicked and retired Gen. Ihejirika. He handed over his government’s security architecture fully back to the North, thus setting the stage for Buhari’s victory at the 2015 presidential election. Apart from appointing Ihejirika the first Igbo Chief of Army Staff, President Jonathan, who owed his 2011 election into the presidency mainly to the sacrifice of the Igbo nation in his favour, also “committed” another unpardonable taboo. He used the Nigerian Army to give Ikemba Odumegwu Ojukwu a full military burial with a 21-gun salute on 2nd March, 2012, at Nnewi. This five-star rite was also accorded Nigeria’s leading fighter for independence and first President, Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe, in November 1996. The Sokoto Caliphate and Arewa cabals see Nigeria as the private estate of their ancestors, and the Army as their ultimate instrument of power over Nigeria. Whatever the votes cannot achieve, the Army will achieve for them. We other Nigerians also claim that Nigeria and the Armed Forces belong to us all, as the Constitution says. But in the end, both Nigeria and its Armed Forces dance to the tune of the Sokoto Caliphate and its Arewa cabals. Indeed, the notion that the Nigerian Army owes more of its allegiance to the Islamic Sokoto Caliphate and Arewa cabals than to the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria is encapsulated in its motto, boldly inscribed in Arabic: “Victory is from Allah alone.” When taken to task, the Army likes to interpret it as “Victory is from God alone” to water down the Islamic overtone. Yet, they vehemently refuse to write it in the Nigerian lingua franca that we all understand, as sanctioned by the Constitution: English. The Army is thus portrayed as a tool of Islam, which is an affront to non-Muslims, particularly Ndi Igbo. We conclude in part two. The post Igbo rebuff of today’s Nigerian Army (I), by Ochereome Nnanna appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Building myths around the NCC Device Checker, by Okoh Aihe
items.description: The NCC Device Checker came on stream on October 7, 2026. Although it was expressly stated that all SIM-enabled devices already connected before the date were automatically verified, with no action needed from the user, I still took my devices through the process of verification by dialing *315#. Here is the result returned for both phones: “This device is NCC Type Approved and verified for use on Nigerian mobile networks.” I needed to be very sure that the backend had been properly sorted before the telecommunications regulator, the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC), could introduce such a very technical process into the regulatory space. It is commonplace for us to see certain things promoted with so much fanfare and bravura, only to find the readiness of such products absolutely wanting. On this particular issue, for me, the NCC may have scored high. “The Device Checker,” according to the regulator, “is an NCC Type Approved service for checking whether a SIM-enabled device model is NCC Type Approved and whether the device is for use on Nigerian mobile networks.” Through the process, the regulator is taking Type Approval a notch higher. “Type Approval is a requirement under Nigerian law that every communications device meets approved technical standards before it is sold or used in the country. It ensures that all device models brought into the country are fit for use in Nigeria. It is prohibited to use, sell or import non-Type Approved communications devices,” the NCC explained. Type Approval is as old as the Communications Act but has been given more impetus now by the regulator in order to clip some subtle features which conspire to degrade the signal quality received by subscribers from the networks. Unfortunately, the fault or failure to receive or connect equipment can easily be classified as network failure. Type Approval is one regulation with which the regulator planned to attack multi-pronged issues. “The integrity of the telecommunications industry depends not only on network infrastructure but also on the quality, safety and compliance of the devices that access and are used on these networks. For this reason, Type Approval is not merely a regulatory requirement. It is a vital mechanism for protecting consumers, safeguarding network performance and preserving confidence in Nigeria’s digital economy,” explained Engr. Edoyemi Ogoh, who is Director, Technical Standards and Network Integrity at NCC. “The initiative,” he continued, “supports the Commission’s broader efforts to strengthen the integrity of devices in Nigeria’s telecommunications sector. It will improve compliance with applicable standards, enhance network performance, facilitate the identification of non-compliant devices, and strengthen consumer confidence in devices sold and used within the country.” The NCC Device Checker has been long in the making, like the meat of the antelope, which takes long to cook in order to achieve maximum delicacy. The regulator said it has consulted with stakeholders across the value chain, which include the Nigeria Customs Service, Original Equipment Manufacturers, importers and relevant market associations, adding that “this collaborative approach reflects our belief that effective regulation is best achieved through partnership, consultation and shared responsibility, consistent with firm belief in collaboration.” In my very simple observation, the regulator is waging a full-fledged war against the grey market through which millions of devices pour into the Nigerian market, phone theft, which is prevalent in this part of the world – a stolen phone can now easily be knocked off the networks – and ensuring the fidelity of products. Phone buyers are investing in genuine products that can deliver proper service by following the International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI) number at the back of the phone pack or even doing the needful to confirm second-hand phones. As one industry source told this writer, this would also mean the Customs Service making more money through revenue generation, because, at the moment, it was possible for cars or buses to be imported into Nigeria with lots of phones in them which are not properly cleared or even have their sources determined, except that their destination is Nigeria. The Device Checker has drawn a line against such practices. Understandably, not everybody is excited about the NCC Device Checker. The Association of Mobile Phones and Allied Products Traders of Nigeria has raised some concerns about the introduction of the Device Checker, asking the NCC to provide a window of sensitisation in order to align all stakeholders with its plans. Even as they support the fight against counterfeit devices, the association is frowning at sundry fees that may be introduced, which could bring more hardship on its members and phone and device buyers. But what is this thing about counterfeit devices? I will tell a personal story. I have an iPad which plays a central role in all my operations. Recently, the charger got bad, and I decided to buy one from a shopping mall nearby before heading out to Banex Plaza to buy an original version the following day. I plugged the iPad with the stop-gap charger and stepped out of the room for some minutes. By the time I returned, the room was charged and very hot. My mind went to the iPad, which was as hot as fire itself. Just a few minutes’ delay, and it would have exploded into a ball of fire. I was lucky because the damage was not extensive. But it still cost about N400,000 to bring it back to life! The nation’s telecommunications sector is growing in leaps and bounds; it therefore demands the attention of the regulator to ensure that such growth is not impaired by fake equipment or allow such equipment to endanger the lives of users. The regulator is waging a war against what the people may ignorantly accept as good and normal, and, in the process, save their lives. Even with all the good attributes of the Device Checker, which could include restoring efficiency to the mobile networks, hyperbolically, and causing subscribers to smile each time a connection is made – oh, thinking of nirvana – I was also very fascinated with what the Device Checker is not, according to the NCC. This is very important in a country where the trust deficit is nearly as important as the country’s legal tender and the politicians are skilled in making falsehood the figment of reality. “The Commission recognizes that consumers have legitimate expectations regarding the privacy and security of their personal information. The Type Approval Compliance framework is not designed for surveillance and does not provide the Commission with access to the content of communications, photographs, messages, contacts, financial information or any other personal information stored on users’ devices. The framework is limited to device identification information required to support regulatory compliance and facilitate the identification of devices that may not meet applicable Type Approval requirements. Consumer privacy remains fully protected in accordance with applicable laws and regulatory requirements,” NCC assured. Such assurances are not misplaced. However, I want to observe that there seems to be a certain urgency in the way the regulator wants to get things done. For long, service quality and network integrity have remained major issues in the regulatory space. The case of the regulator, therefore, can be likened to that of a man fighting fire desperately. I implore relevant stakeholders to give the regulator the needed help in order to create an industry that may bring benefits to all. The post Building myths around the NCC Device Checker, by Okoh Aihe appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: The Three Dates for Deciding Ukraine’s Future
items.description: O ver the next eight weeks , as winter envelopes Ukraine, Russia plans to use the frigid weather as a weapon. Its arms factories have already made enough missiles and drones to take down Ukraine’s electrical grid, as well as the heating systems that millions of people rely on to stay warm. Homes far from the front will become deadly for their inhabitants as temperatures fall. In that same time frame, three events taking place thousands of miles away could determine Ukraine’s future. The first is America’s Election Day, now two weeks away; leaders in Kyiv fear that if Democrats win one or both chambers of Congress, President Trump may turn even further against them in those final weeks of full Republican control of Washington. The second is a proposed summit in mid-November in southern China, where Russian President Vladimir Putin wants to meet with Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping to plan how to end the war—without having a seat at the table for Ukraine. The third is the G20 summit at Trump’s Miami-area golf course, scheduled to take place in mid-December. The president has visions of standing between Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky as they sign a peace deal, even if he has to strong-arm Ukraine to do it, according to advisers. One Ukrainian official, speaking on the condition of anonymity to candidly discuss internal conversations, told us that it’s hard not to feel left out of decision making that will dictate the country’s future: “It looks like this is all happening without us.” The U.S. president, who used to brag that he could resolve the war in 24 hours, has tossed aside some sanctions on Russia and struck a deal with Putin to import diesel from Moscow, giving a boost to the Russian war machine. He and his allies have threatened Kyiv, demanding that Zelensky stop attacking Russian oil refineries or risk losing access to American intelligence, weaponry, and satellite communications that it uses to defend itself. The calendar is now Ukraine’s foe—and so, Ukrainians fear, is Donald Trump. T rump’s war in Iran has appeared to throttle Republicans’ chances in the midterms; the unending conflict, and the resulting surge in oil and gas prices, has eroded the GOP’s poll numbers and fueled Democrats’ hopes of taking both chambers of Congress. Stymied in his efforts to bring that war to a close, Trump recently shifted his focus to resolving the Ukraine conflict, in part to bring fuel prices down. But the way he’s chosen to try to do that has provided his fellow Republicans with a nasty October surprise . In a first for a U.S. president, Trump has sided with a traditional adversary, Russia, over a democracy that is not only fighting for its existence but also acting as a bulwark against a wider war. Trump’s diesel deal with Putin will have a negligible impact on American energy prices, but it’s a financial lifeline for Moscow. [ Read: Ukraine finds a new set of targets ] Trump has demanded an energy cease-fire—he even announced one earlier this month that had no basis in reality—yet has focused his ire entirely on Ukraine’s attacks on Russian oil refineries. He blames those strikes for the rise in energy prices while ignoring the real culprit, Iran’s ability to defy the United States and close the Strait of Hormuz . He’s convinced himself, three people close to him have told us, that Ukraine’s attacks on the refineries are, in part, meant to undermine Republicans’ chances next month—and, by extension, Trump. The president has ignored Moscow’s attacks on Ukraine’s electrical grid, and yesterday, hours after a drone strike on a public park killed six people, including two children, he downplayed its strikes on Ukraine’s cities, declaring that Russia had not “been doing much.” An image of one of the dead children, a 1-year-old killed as she sat in her stroller, was broadcast around the globe. More pressure could be coming. Trump aides have threatened to withhold arms sales unless Kyiv stops targeting Russian diesel plants; this week, the administration delayed approving the transfer of missiles that Ukraine needs for its defense. Ukraine in the past week has said that it has not consistently received early warnings of attacks and no longer has full Starshield satellite access, which is impeding its ability to defend itself against Russia’s new fleet of jet-powered drones. ( The Wall Street Journal reported today that Starshield’s creator, Elon Musk, ordered the slowdown . The White House and Musk had previously denied involvement.) Some in Trump’s orbit have suggested that the United States go further and stop sharing intelligence with Ukraine. Trump’s deference to Putin has been a theme for a decade, yet this new round of kowtowing has handed Republicans another obstacle ahead of the elections. In a rare act of defiance, a handful in the party have denounced the president’s decisions, including his move to undercut a Russia-sanctions bill that he signed only a month ago in honor of its champion, the late Senator Lindsey Graham. The quick betrayal of Graham’s legacy was a blow for some of his Senate colleagues; GOP aides told us that Graham’s sudden July death cost Ukraine its most vocal champion in Trump’s inner circle, and that no one has stepped up to fill that void. Michael Froman, who worked in the Clinton and Obama administrations and is now president of the Council on Foreign Relations, told us that cutting off Kyiv from American weapons or intelligence might, in fact, prolong the war because it “would undermine Ukraine’s position at the negotiating table and make it less likely Russia would be willing to negotiate on any of the key outstanding issues.” Officials with both parties predict that the Democrats will capture the House next month; the Senate appears to be a true toss-up. Kyiv will be carefully watching the results. A Democratic win next month will, in the long run, likely help Kyiv, and some of the more hopeful members of Zelensky’s camp believe that Republican defeats could force Trump to focus more on domestic issues, resulting in him leaving Ukraine alone. But other observers on both sides of the Atlantic fear that the opposite could be true. A president without a friendly Congress tends to fall back more on foreign policy, where he needs little help from Capitol Hill. Either way, the new Congress won’t be seated until January 3, leaving Trump unchecked for two more months and perhaps motivated to wield power before his party moves into the minority. Another major national election would not be for two years—plenty of time for Trump to push Ukraine without fear of voters punishing Republicans. “He could get distracted at any time,” one outside Trump ally told us. “But right now, he’s furious at Ukraine, and he wants Zelensky gone.” T wo weeks after Election Day , Trump plans to board Air Force One bound for a series of summits in Asia. Earlier this month, Trump overruled White House aides who had counseled against him calling to wish Putin a happy birthday, warning that little good would come of it. In that conversation, Trump authorized the diesel deal, and Putin suggested something grander: a meeting of the world’s great powers to divide up the world. Or at least Ukraine. Putin proposed that he, Trump, and Xi hold a trilateral meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation in Shenzhen, China, in mid-November to discuss a variety of issues, including Ukraine. Trump told reporters yesterday that he is open to attending the meeting, which would be his first face-to-face encounter with Putin since their unproductive summit in Alaska last year. It is no surprise that Trump is drawn to the idea; his deference toward Putin is rivaled only by his regard for Xi, whom he hosted in lavish fashion at the White House last month. He has previously been intrigued by the idea of the three powers—China, Russia, the United States—dividing the globe into spheres of influence, although Moscow these days hardly wields the international clout of Washington or Beijing. [ Read: The deferential president ] The idea of two authoritarians and their admirer plotting to slice up sovereign nations alarmed much of the West. And how, Kyiv demanded, could Ukraine’s future be decided with no input from Ukraine? But some in Trump’s orbit have backed the idea, belittling Ukraine as a corrupt backwater with no autonomy. Putin has never viewed Ukraine as a legitimate country, and Trump has held a grudge against it since 2019, when he was impeached (for the first time) after pressuring Zelensky to dig up damaging information about Trump’s political rival Joe Biden. He and his Ukrainian counterpart had a shouting match at the White House early in Trump’s second term, causing the U.S. to briefly withhold intelligence. Since then, Zelensky has tried to flatter Trump to stay on his good side, but those niceties have vanished as the American president has demanded that Ukraine pick a new leader. Many of those in Trump’s orbit are unsympathetic to Ukraine’s plight and see the war not as a battle for the modern, rules-based world order—with its cardinal tenet prohibiting the seizure of land by force—but as an impediment to future business deals with Russia, some of which could enrich members of the president’s inner circle. Pushing Ukraine into taking a deal, even if that means it has to give up its claim on the Donbas, would open up avenues to dealmaking on Russia’s diesel, rare-earth minerals, and other resources. Zelensky has balked at any territorial concessions. “Our worry is that they are looking at this as a new Yalta Conference, to divide the world into spheres of influence,” another Ukrainian official told us. Trump’s ideal timeline for some sort of Russia-Ukraine peace agreement, as we reported last week, would be in December at the G20 summit. That bit of history, were it to occur, would take place at one of Trump’s own properties. In Trump’s first term, he pushed to host the 2020 G7 at his golf course in Doral, just outside of Miami. But Trump abandoned the idea amid bipartisan blowback over his plan to personally profit off the event. This time, there has been nary a Republican whimper of protest about Trump’s venue choice, but some have lodged complaints about the president’s other idea for the summit: to invite Putin. The Russian leader has yet to agree to show up, but if he does, it would be the first time he has attended a multilateral summit in a Western country since his invasion of Ukraine. It would allow him to take another step in shedding his status as an international pariah, though it is hard to imagine that European leaders are eager to talk with Putin. Zelensky, who has already committed to attending the G20, has made clear that he would be willing to sit down with Putin, no matter the venue, to work out an agreement to end the war. If Trump has his way over the next eight weeks, it might be not a negotiation, but a capitulation.

items.title: Kashim Shettima’s response in kind to Atiku Abubakar, by Rotimi Fasan
items.description: It’s exactly a week ago today that the All Progressives Congress inaugurated its expanded Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) at the presidential villa in Abuja. It was an occasion for some chest-thumping as well as an opportunity for the APC to set out its agenda for the 2027 campaigns. As is to be expected, the inauguration of the APC’s PCC presented Nigerians, including opposition politicians and their supporters, yet another opportunity to scrutinise the APC-led Bola Tinubu administration. That scrutiny has appropriately come with criticisms of the government’s performance or the person of the president. The APC leadership had itself set the ball rolling by responding in kind to recent attacks on the party beginning with the ADC’s presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar’s ill-advised decision, to address President Bola Tinubu by his first name at formal public events. It was a gesture that many Nigerians advised the former vice president to desist from. Not only is it a breach of protocol, it is also culturally distasteful. But since it appeared to be getting him the needed attention, no matter how negative, from a section of the public, Atiku chose to double down on it and recruited his surrogates into the Tinubu-baiting game. The likes of Paul Ibe and Phrank Shaibu thought they were being dutiful by joining their principal to go the street-fighter route forgetting that they did not own the patent for retailing insults to political opponents. It was therefore not surprising to see Vice President Kashim Shettima use the occasion of the inauguration of his party’s PCC to launch a number of broadsides at both Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi of the NDC. In his words, ‘We have the capacity to respond to all sorts of innuendoes and outright lies that our political opponents are taking on’. This is precisely what Nigerians who cautioned Alhaji Atiku Abubakar and his co-travellers feared would happen. They were starting a fire they would not be able to put out. One that would downgrade the quality of the campaign and deflect attention from the type of issues the candidates should be addressing. Shettima’s verbal shots are not new. Some of them are old arrows seasoned with new baits. Apparently referencing Atiku Abubakar’s displeasure to similar verbal shots in the past, he started by asking those who come to equity to do so with clean hands. He then went on to tell his audience that President Bola Tinubu remained the President and Commander-in-Chief of Nigeria no matter what Atiku chose to call him. Whether Bola or Adekunle, it made no difference he said. Atiku’s repeated contestation for the presidency, he argued, only made him a Raila Odinga, a former Prime Minister in Kenya, who repeatedly contested but failed to be president and not an Abraham Lincoln who eventually succeeded after several failed attempts at contesting to be president in America. Speaking rather tongue in cheek, he said he would not ‘follow suit with Lawal and call him Kachalla’ by which he recalled Babachir Lawal’s reference to Atiku as Kachalla, which is a word for a leader of bandits in the north. In Shettima’s attack on Atiku, Peter Obi of the Nigeria Democratic Congress suffered what one might call a collateral damage. Shettima called Obi ‘the master of bogus statistics and incoherent economic prescriptions’ from Bangladesh. Policies that worked in Bangladesh, he said quite correctly, would not automatically work in Nigeria with a demographic, economic and institutional structures that are vastly different. I have called the damage Obi suffered from Shettima’s attack as collateral only because, unlike the attack on Atiku, it came unprovoked. At least not by anything Obi had said or done to the APC or its leadership in the immediate context of the point at issue. Obi is, however, as guilty as Atiku when it comes to such matters. The only difference is that as the master of performative morality and mob incitement, Peter Obi leaves the dirty work of rage baits and cussing to his Obidient followers. Some of them, like the shawl-wearing Edo-pretend, who contributes nothing aimed at intellectual or policy direction for her principal, cusses worse than an infidel. She is always invoking Ogun to ‘kpai’ her political opponents. What type of vote-canvassing is that? Yet what rankles in all of this has been the response of supporters of Atiku Abubakar. Their latest criticism of Shettima’s attack of their principal is utterly hypocritical. It harks back to what Atiku himself had said in the past when Shettima took the verbal war to him. Atiku had said he would not respond to Shettima because he was older and more accomplished than him. Shettima’s utterances he said breached northern codes of respect for elders. Which again should tell Nigerians about the ADC’s presidential candidate’s style of politics which operates by appealing to religious and ethnic sentiments. He is a politician who wants Bola Tinubu’s job for himself and is bent on handing Shettima’s job to Rotimi Ameachi (in 2023 it was Ifeanyin Okowa), where does age much less regional or ethnic consideration come into the debate? If Atiku ‘Tarkaed’ Shettima and Shettima ‘Dabohed’ him, should that offend God? You push me, I push you. Why should Alhaji Abubakar’s response be about northern solidarity? Why is he struggling to address the point raised by Shettima on its merit? Does it mean Tinubu is good target because he is from the south? Which Nigerian or foreign culture preaches outright the disrespect of elders? Nigerians should ask Atiku and his followers why they think it is appropriate for them to address the president by his first name at formal events but chafe at the ‘duba-gari’ tag that Shettima has foisted on him? Afterall, duba-gari is not a curse. It is the Hausa equivalent of ‘wole-wole’, the Yoruba word for a sanitary inspector. As Phrank Shaibu asked Seun Okinbaloye if Bola is not the president’s name to justify their action of calling him by his first name, so can any Nigerian ask if Atiku did not train as a sanitary inspector? He did attend the Kano School of Hygiene! Should things like this be the talking point of the 2027 campaigns? Of course, no! But it’s the path Atiku chose to walk with his surrogates and it can’t be right for them and then be wrong for Shettima because he is of the APC. Taunts and puns are a critical part of political rhetoric. They could be a source of entertainment as well as education when rightly deployed. Thus, they have their place in politics and Nigeria has had past masters of the art like S.L.A. Akintola and K.O. Mbadiwe among others. At a time of grave economic and social disjunction, however, they should not constitute the main subject of national debate. The post Kashim Shettima’s response in kind to Atiku Abubakar, by Rotimi Fasan appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Le gouvernement vise la création d’un million d’emplois d’ici 2031
items.description: Le nouveau gouvernement a déclaré que la stratégie sur laquelle il mise, fondée sur une dynamique intégrée associant le renforcement de la compétitivité des secteurs productifs et des services, la valorisation de leurs atouts, la stimulation de l’investissement et le renforcement de la production locale, pourrait ouvrir de nouvelles perspectives en matière de croissance et d’emploi. Cette approche permettrait de créer près d’un million d’emplois au cours de son mandat. Le gouvernement dirigé par le Parti authenticité et modernité (PAM) reprend cet engagement dans son programme électoral présenté lors des élections législatives de 2026. Il s’agit d’un objectif que le gouvernement sortant d’Aziz Akhannouch n’a pas atteint, alors même qu’il figurait parmi les dix engagements inscrits dans le programme gouvernemental du précédent mandat, couvrant la période 2021-2026. S’agissant des détails du programme gouvernemental pour le nouveau mandat 2026-2031, celui-ci prévoit notamment de porter le taux d’activité économique des femmes à 21,2 %, afin de ramener le taux de chômage à 7 % à l’horizon 2031. Cet objectif figurait également dans le programme électoral du parti arrivé en tête, qui a obtenu 97 sièges lors des dernières élections législatives. Selon le document consulté par le média Hespress, les emplois à créer se répartissent comme suit : 250 000 emplois nets dans l’industrie, 80 000 emplois destinés à de jeunes agriculteurs résidents, 40 000 emplois dans le secteur sportif, ainsi que 270 000 emplois dans les services délocalisés à forte valeur ajoutée. À cela s’ajoutent 360 000 emplois liés à l’organisation de la Coupe du monde 2030 et aux activités connexes à caractère productif et de services. Concernant le développement du tissu coopératif et le soutien à l’économie sociale et solidaire, le gouvernement indique que ce secteur connaît une « dynamique importante ». Il compte plus de 65 000 coopératives employant environ 800 000 personnes. Le gouvernement précise : « Malgré le potentiel considérable du secteur en matière de création d’emplois et de renforcement de la cohésion sociale et territoriale, cette dynamique se heurte à plusieurs contraintes structurelles. Celles-ci résident principalement dans la faiblesse de la structuration économique, les limites en matière de gouvernance, les difficultés d’accès au financement et aux marchés, ainsi que la faible intégration dans les chaînes de valeur. En outre, 93 % des coopératives demeurent de petites structures fragiles. » Dans ce contexte, l’approche du gouvernement consiste à « faire des coopératives un véritable levier de développement territorial, de création de richesse et de préservation durable des emplois », à travers deux axes principaux. Le premier vise à consolider le tissu coopératif et à assurer sa pérennité. Il a pour objectif de transformer les coopératives en structures économiques durables, capables de créer de la valeur et de préserver les emplois. Selon le programme, cet objectif sera poursuivi « par le renforcement du cadre juridique et de la gouvernance, la structuration des coopératives à travers leur intégration dans des unions et des réseaux coopératifs, ainsi que par le développement de leurs capacités et leur accompagnement dans le domaine de la numérisation ». Cet axe prévoit également l’amélioration de la productivité et des chaînes de valeur, la facilitation de la commercialisation et de l’accès aux marchés, ainsi que l’amélioration de l’accès au financement. Le deuxième axe porte sur « la mise en place d’un nouveau modèle de création de coopératives, fondé sur une logique de ciblage intelligent et territorial, afin de renforcer leur impact social et économique ». Il s’agira notamment de « privilégier les zones caractérisées par une forte vulnérabilité sociale et les catégories de population les plus exposées à l’exclusion économique ». Le nouvel exécutif souligne enfin que ce programme accorde la priorité aux jeunes qui ne sont ni scolarisés, ni en formation, ni en emploi, ainsi qu’aux personnes en situation de handicap, aux femmes en situation de précarité et aux populations du monde rural. The post Le gouvernement vise la création d’un million d’emplois d’ici 2031 appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Obuasi SHTS: Safeguarding breaches leave teachers exposed to disputed allegations – Safeguarding Officer
items.description: Safeguarding failures leave students vulnerable, and teachers exposed when allegations arise, Amartei K. Amartey, Safeguarding Officer at Kingsdale Secondary Schools in the UK, has warned. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Tuesday, he said professional boundaries protect both children and school staff. He argued that asking a female student to deliver food to a staff member’s residence breaches those boundaries. His comments followed allegations of sexual abuse at Obuasi Senior High Technical School and questions about how education authorities handled complaints. “Why is a girl child carrying food to a staff member’s house? That’s a safeguarding issue. That’s a red flag,” he said. For Mr Amartey, the danger extends beyond the errand itself. Such situations place children in vulnerable positions and leave staff struggling to defend themselves when accounts of an encounter differ. “Why have you broken the number one rule, which is safeguarding—not just safeguarding for the child, but for you, the member of staff as well?” He questioned how staff could protect themselves against disputed allegations after disregarding the rules designed to prevent such encounters. “The teacher or this member of staff is claiming they are innocent. What is their evidence?” Mr Amartey said compliance with safeguarding procedures was central to avoiding conflicting accounts. “How do you mitigate he say, she say by following the rules? And you broke the rule.” Asked whether a teacher in the UK could send a child from the dining hall to the teacher’s residence with food, he replied: “Never. You won’t even dream about it.” He said such conduct could carry serious consequences in the UK. “You will lose your license and possibly be charged.” Mr Amartey also criticised the committee’s handling of the matter. He argued that the safeguarding breach should itself have demanded action. “For me, it’s just been a waste of time.” The controversy follows Manasseh Azure Awuni’s JoyNews documentary, Inside the Dreaded Headmaster’s Bungalow . It examines allegations of sexual abuse involving the school’s headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai. The Ghana Education Service says the headmaster remains interdicted. It has also directed the Ashanti Regional and Obuasi Municipal education directors to step aside while investigations continue. The allegations against the headmaster remain under investigation.

items.title: Diphtérie: Une masterclass organisée à Rabat pour la détection et la prise en charge
items.description: Le groupement sanitaire territorial de Rabat-Salé-Kénitra (GST-RSK), à travers la GST Academy, organise, du 22 au 24 octobre à l'hôpital d'enfants de Rabat, une masterclass consacrée à la « détection et à la prise en charge d'un cas de diphtérie ». Cette initiative s'inscrit dans le cadre du renforcement des compétences des professionnels de santé et de l’amélioration des capacités de préparation et de réponse aux urgences sanitaires, indique le GST-RSK dans un communiqué. Elle s'inscrit également dans une démarche de renforcement de la veille et de la sécurité sanitaires, et vise à améliorer les capacités des professionnels de santé à reconnaître de manière précoce les cas suspects de diphtérie, à déclencher les dispositifs d’alerte appropriés et à assurer une prise en charge rapide, efficace et coordonnée face au risque épidémique, ajoute la même source. La cérémonie d’ouverture de cette session de formation se tiendra jeudi, en présence du directeur général du GST-RSK, le professeur Brahim Lekehal, qui présentera les objectifs et les enjeux de cette initiative. Destinée aux professionnels de santé susceptibles d'intervenir dans la gestion d’une alerte épidémique, notamment les médecins, les infirmiers, les urgentistes, les hygiénistes, les biologistes et les épidémiologistes, cette masterclass s’appuie sur une approche pédagogique interactive combinant apports théoriques, démonstrations pratiques et exercices de simulation. Durant les trois journées de formation, les participants examineront les différentes étapes de la gestion d’une alerte de diphtérie, depuis la surveillance épidémiologique et la détection précoce des cas suspects jusqu’à la confirmation biologique, l’évaluation des risques, la prise en charge des patients et la mise en œuvre des mesures de riposte sanitaire appropriées, précise le communiqué, notant qu'une attention particulière sera accordée à la communication sur les risques sanitaires, à la sensibilisation communautaire et à la coordination des équipes d’intervention. S’inscrivant dans une approche de formation des formateurs, cette initiative ambitionne également de favoriser la diffusion des connaissances acquises et le partage des bonnes pratiques au sein des structures de santé, contribuant ainsi au renforcement durable des capacités régionales de préparation et de réponse aux menaces épidémiques. À travers l’organisation de cette masterclass, le GST-RSK, via la GST Academy, réaffirme son engagement en faveur du développement continu des compétences des professionnels de santé, du renforcement de la vigilance sanitaire et de l'amélioration de la qualité et de la sécurité des soins, au service de la protection de la santé de la population, conclut le communiqué. The post Diphtérie: Une masterclass organisée à Rabat pour la détection et la prise en charge appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: ‘One or two teachers in almost every school engage in sexual misconduct’ — Teacher alleges
items.description: A teacher at Ekumpoano Catholic Basic School, Stephen Desu, has alleged that sexual misconduct by teachers is widespread across Ghana’s schools, claiming that almost every school has one or two teachers involved in such behaviour. He said the problem had persisted for years but was often not openly acknowledged, warning that failure to confront it decisively could leave students vulnerable to abuse. “ And almost every school, if all of us will be politically correct with everything, everybody is aware that in almost every school, there is one or there are two teachers who are engaged in this,” he said. Mr Desu made the comments on Joy News’ PM Express on Tuesday, October 20, during a discussion on allegations of sexual abuse involving female students at Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS). The case has drawn national attention following reports by JoyNews investigative correspondent Manasseh Azure Awuni. The school’s headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai, has been interdicted by the Ghana Education Service (GES) and arrested by the police as investigations continue. The allegations against Mr Abdulai have not been established in court. ‘The problem is at every level’ Mr Desu said sexual misconduct was not confined to senior high schools, adding that concerns existed at the primary and junior high school levels as well. “At the primary level, the problem is there. At the JHS level, it’s there. But it’s worse. It’s worse at the SHS level,” he said. He also alleged that some teachers viewed postings to senior high schools as an opportunity to engage in sexual misconduct. “And sometimes a teacher will be at a primary school and say, no, I wish to go to the SHS. Why? Because that’s where he can exhibit his predatory, you know, sexual misbehaviour,” he said. Asked whether colleagues made such comments, he replied: “Of course.” Calls for accountability Mr Desu blamed what he described as the failure of the GES to deal decisively with sexual misconduct for allowing the problem to persist. He argued that when people were not punished for wrongdoing, others could be encouraged to repeat the behaviour. “And any time you have a situation where people are not punished for wrongdoing, it begins to fester. And more people learn from that misbehaviour and continue to do the wrong things. And a lot of people copy,” he said. He called for a more decisive response from education authorities, particularly in dealing with complaints and ensuring that students were protected. The allegations surrounding Obuasi SHTS have renewed scrutiny of how schools respond to complaints of sexual misconduct and whether existing safeguards adequately protect students. Mr Desu’s claim that such behaviour occurs in almost every school was not independently substantiated in the interview comments provided. The GES and other relevant authorities would need to establish the extent of the problem through credible evidence and investigations.

items.title: Une Sidwaya du 21-10-2026
Journées régionales de l’agro-écologie des Tannounyan La Ire édition se tiendra les 22 et 23 octobre prochains à Banfora
items.description: La 1re édition des journées régionales de l’agroécologie des Tannounyan se tiendront, les 22 et 23 octobre prochains, à Banfora sur le thème « Agroécologie et résilience des communautés : stratégies et leviers d’action ». Les organisateurs ont annoncé les couleurs de l’évènement à travers une conférence de presse, le lundi 19 octobre 2026, dans la cité du Paysan noir. L’agroécologie va être à l’honneur, les 22 et 23 octobre, à Banfora. La ville va abriter en effet la Ire édition des journées régionales de l’agro-écologie des Tannounyan. L’information a été donnée par les organisateurs de l’évènement à travers une conférence de presse qu’ils ont animée dans l’après-midi du lundi 19 octobre 2026, dans la cité du Paysan noir. Le thème retenu est « Agroécologie et résilience des communautés : stratégies et leviers d’action ». Le principal conférencier, Larissa Kaboré, a indiqué que ces journées sont organisées par l’association Munyu des femmes, en collaboration avec la commune de Banfora, le Conseil national de l’agriculture biologique et le Cadre de concertation des acteurs de l’agroécologie et de l’agriculture biologique des Tannounyan. A l’écouter, l’évènement s’inscrit dans la continuité des journées nationales de l’agro-écologie dont la IIe édition s’est tenue en décembre 2025, et visent à prolonger cette dynamique à l’échelle régionale. Face aux défis auxquels font face les communautés tels que les changements climatiques et la dégradation des ressources naturelles, a-t-elle expliqué, l’agro-écologie offre des pistes d’actions pour renforcer la capacité des communautés à y faire face. Mais la transition agroécologique, a-t-elle poursuivi, outre les techniques agricoles, nécessite également une meilleure information des populations, la mobilisation des acteurs territoriaux et l’engagement de tous. Ces journées visent donc aux dires de Larissa Kaboré, à permettre aux acteurs des Tannounyan de s’approprier les enjeux liés à l’agro-écologie de partager leurs expériences et d’identifier des solutions adaptées à leurs réalités. Cela, avec pour objectif globale, de renforcer la résilience des communautés par la valorisation du potentiel agroécologique dans la région. Durant ce rendez-vous de deux jours, plusieurs communications et une mini-foire sont au menu. Des communications qui vont porter sur,entre autres thèmes, « Stratégie nationale de développement de l’agroécologie : acquis et perspectives », et « Agroécologie, recherche et innovation : leviers d’action pour la résilience des communautés ». Quant à la mini-foire, elle va permettre de mettre un point d’honneur sur les produits, les initiatives et les savoir-faire des acteurs régionaux. Quelles ambitions nourrit cet évènement à moyen et long terme ? A cette question de la presse, Mme Kaboré a confié qu’à long terme il vise la transition agroécologique, afin que les pratiques agroécologiques soient adoptées par les producteurs et par toute la communauté et que les produits agroécologiques le soient aussi par les consommateurs. Séance tenante, les conférenciers ont appelé les producteurs, les transformateurs, les organisations professionnelles, les organisations de la société civile et les services techniques, à se mobiliser pour la réussite de ces journées. Alpha Sékou BARRY alphasekoubarry@gmail.com

items.title: Superhighway: Ebonyi Community demands compliance with Umahi’s directive on borrow pits
items.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The people of Ndiebor Ishieke Autonomous Community in Ebonyi Local Government Area of Ebonyi State have called for strict compliance with the directive of the Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi, on borrow-pit operations along the ongoing Calabar–Ebonyi–Enugu-Benue–Nasarawa–Abuja Superhighway project. The community urged the relevant authorities and the project contractor to ensure that further excavation activities complied with the minister’s directive, particularly regarding landowners’ consent, consultation with host communities and the protection of farmlands and economic crops. The stakeholders, who commended Umahi for his intervention over concerns about alleged damage to agricultural lands in the area, said effective enforcement of the directive was necessary to safeguard rural livelihoods, prevent further encroachment and avert avoidable disputes between affected residents and the project authorities. The community in a joint statement signed by the traditional ruler of Ndiebor Ishieke Autonomous Community, Eze Hyacinth Awoke Nwiboko; the President of the community. They acknowledged the interventions and contributions of Ebonyi State Governor, Francis Nwifuru, and Senator Peter Nwebonyi, representing Ebonyi North Senatorial District, towards addressing the concerns associated with the project. They, however, maintained that the minister’s directive must translate into concrete measures to protect affected landowners and ensure that construction activities were conducted in accordance with the relevant safeguards. According to the statement, the community supports the superhighway project because of its potential to improve transportation, facilitate the movement of agricultural produce and other goods, and stimulate economic development across the benefiting states. The stakeholders nevertheless cautioned that the pursuit of infrastructure development should not undermine the property rights, economic security and environmental safety of host communities. “Our community supports the superhighway project and recognises its potential to boost transportation, trade and economic development. However, we maintain that infrastructure development must respect the land rights, agricultural livelihoods and environmental safety of host communities,” the statement said. The community expressed concern over reports of damage to farmlands and economic crops, noting that agriculture remained a major source of livelihood for many households in the area. It identified yam, cassava, rice, millet and beniseed among the crops cultivated by residents, warning that the destruction of productive farmland could worsen the economic difficulties of affected farming families. The stakeholders consequently called for a transparent assessment of the alleged losses and appropriate compensation for verified damage to crops, farmland and other legitimate property interests arising from the excavation activities. They also urged the relevant authorities to establish effective communication channels involving traditional institutions, community representatives, landowners, project supervisors and the contractor before further borrow-pit operations were undertaken. The community leaders said prior consultation and timely communication would help prevent misunderstandings, promote mutual trust and ensure that legitimate grievances were addressed before they escalated into disputes. They further called for the reclamation of abandoned or exhausted borrow pits and the implementation of adequate environmental safeguards to protect residents, agricultural land and the surrounding ecosystem from hazards associated with excavation activities. The signatories stressed that transparent procedures for assessing affected properties and determining compensation were essential to securing the cooperation of host communities and sustaining public confidence in the project. On the broader development concerns, the community commended Governor Nwifuru for his administration’s development efforts in Ebonyi State and acknowledged Senator Nwebonyi’s representation of the district, including his reported legislative contributions towards attracting the superhighway project. They appealed to both public officials to sustain their engagement with the relevant federal authorities to ensure that the concerns of affected residents received appropriate attention. The statement added that the successful implementation of the project required a balance between the Federal Government’s infrastructure objectives and the legitimate interests of communities whose lands were affected by construction activities. Reaffirming their commitment to peaceful engagement, the traditional ruler and other signatories pledged the community’s cooperation with the Federal Government, the Ebonyi State Government, the Ministry of Works and the contractor in finding a lasting resolution to the concerns. “Our position is clear: we support the superhighway project, but development must not come at the expense of our land rights, livelihoods and environmental safety,” the statement added. The stakeholders expressed hope that compliance with Umahi’s directive would lead to practical measures to protect affected landowners, address outstanding compensation claims and ensure that construction activities proceeded without unnecessary conflict with host communities. items.title: Ebonyi arrest 30 suspected sex workers
items.description: ….seals unapproved guest house By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The Ebonyi State Ministry of Capital City and Urban Planning has arrested 30 suspected sex workers over alleged security concerns and the discovery of suspected hard drugs at the premises in a guest house in Abakaliki. The team also sealed the Guest House in Abakaliki following an inspection of unapproved building used as guest House. The Commissioner for Capital City and Urban Planning, Hon. Richard Ugo Idike, in collaboration with the Commissioner for Internal Security, Hon. Prince Etta Uka Ude, alongside security operatives and members of the ministry’s taskforce carried out the operation. Addressing journalists during the inspection, Hon. Idike expressed concern over the alleged security threats associated with activities at the guest house. He noted that the presence of individuals reportedly from different states had raised concerns about security and public safety in the area. The Commissioner disclosed that the team discovered substances suspected to be hard drugs, including wrappers allegedly containing substances locally referred to as Colos and Indian hemp, among others. The suspected substances were reportedly recovered during the operation, while security operatives took charge of the matter. Idike reiterated the state government’s commitment to ensuring that buildings within Abakaliki are used for lawful purposes and comply with approved development plans. He called on property developers and building owners to obtain the necessary building approvals from the Ministry of Capital City and Urban Planning before commencing construction, stressing that the government would not tolerate the use of unapproved buildings for activities that could threaten public safety. The Commissioner subsequently directed that Guest House be sealed indefinitely pending further clarification and compliance with the ministry’s requirements. He also directed the owner of the facility to visit the ministry to explain the circumstances surrounding the building and resolve the outstanding issues The Commissioner for Internal Security, Hon. Prince Etta Uka Ude, in his remarks said the primary concern of his ministry was to ensure adequate security and protect residents of Ebonyi State. He stated that the state government would not tolerate the use of any premises as a haven for criminal activities. Ude added that the Ebonyi State Government, under the leadership of governor Francis Ogbonna Nwifuru, remained committed to maintaining peace, law and order across the state. He urged security agencies to intensify surveillance and monitoring of establishments suspected of engaging in illegal activities, particularly within Abakaliki, to prevent criminal elements from exploiting business premises to undermine public safety. The Commissioner stressed the importance of collaboration between government agencies, security operatives and members of the public in identifying and addressing security threats. At the time of filing this report, the over 30 arrested individuals had reportedly been taken into police custody for further investigation, while the owner of the Guest House had yet to be arrested. The sealing of the facility underscores the state government’s enforcement efforts concerning building regulations, public safety and security within the capital city. The post Ebonyi arrest 30 suspected sex workers appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 2027: Ebonyi Stakeholders’ Summit endorses Nwifuru for Second Term
items.description: …Adopts zoning arrangement, calls for peaceful election By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The Ebonyi State Leaders and Stakeholders’ Political Summit has endorsed Governor Francis Nwifuru for a second term in office ahead of the 2027 governorship election. The endorsement was made through a unanimous voice vote at the summit held on Tuesday at the Ecumenical Centre, Abakaliki, following a motion moved by the senator representing Ebonyi North, Onyekachi Nwebonyi. The summit, which brought together political leaders and stakeholders from the three senatorial zones and 13 local government areas of the state, was held under the theme, “Orderly and Peaceful Political Transition in Ebonyi State: The Way Forward.” Among those who attended were the first civilian governor of the state, Senator Sam Egwu; former Senate President Anyim Pius Anyim; former governor Martin Elechi; former governor and Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi; and Nwifuru, who attended as Special Guest of Honour. The stakeholders deliberated on the future of the state, with particular emphasis on political stability, zoning, equity, continuity in governance and the need for a peaceful transition ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a communiqué issued at the end of the summit, the participants reaffirmed their commitment to peace, unity and political stability, describing them as essential to the continued development of Ebonyi. The communiqué, which was read by Mrs Chioma Nweze, was signed by Umahi, Anyim, Egwu and other leaders present on behalf of the summit. They called on political leaders, public office holders, traditional rulers, religious leaders, civil society organisations and citizens to protect the state’s unity, irrespective of political affiliation and other differences. The summit urged political parties, aspirants and their supporters to conduct their activities with restraint and mutual respect, while rejecting inflammatory rhetoric, intimidation, political violence and other actions capable of disrupting public order. On the contentious issue of zoning, the summit expressed support for the continuation of the governorship rotation arrangement among the three senatorial zones, saying the practice had helped promote inclusion and political stability since the beginning of the Fourth Republic in 1999. The communiqué noted that the state’s first three elected governors — Egwu from Ebonyi North, Elechi from Ebonyi Central and Umahi from Ebonyi South — each served two four-year terms. It said the arrangement had encouraged continuity, mutual accommodation and respect for established political understandings among the zones. The summit consequently resolved that Ebonyi North should complete the governorship slot in the 2027 electoral cycle, in line with the zoning principle recognised by the participants. It further proposed that the governorship should move to Ebonyi Central in 2031 and remain there for eight years before moving to Ebonyi South in 2039 for another eight years. The proposed rotation schedule provides for Ebonyi North from 2023 to 2031, Ebonyi Central from 2031 to 2039 and Ebonyi South from 2039 to 2047. The stakeholders also called for the equitable distribution of public amenities and development projects among the zones, stressing the need to sustain fairness, justice and peaceful coexistence. On governance, the summit commended Nwifuru’s administration for its development initiatives under the People’s Charter of Needs. It identified infrastructure and rural development, education, healthcare, agriculture, food security, human capital development, women’s empowerment and youth development as important areas requiring sustained attention. The summit urged political leaders and other stakeholders to continue promoting dialogue across party lines and discourage actions capable of creating unnecessary tension during the transition period. It also called on political parties, aspirants, security agencies, electoral authorities and the media to work towards peaceful, credible and orderly elections in 2027. The participants urged politicians to pursue their ambitions through lawful and democratic means, respect the rights of other citizens, avoid hate speech and misinformation, and recognise the role of relevant institutions in electoral matters. The communiqué expressed appreciation to the leaders and representatives of the 13 local government areas, political parties and community organisations who participated in the deliberations. It reaffirmed the summit’s aspiration for an Ebonyi State that remains peaceful, united, inclusive and development-oriented, while urging leaders and citizens to translate the resolutions into practical commitments that would advance the welfare of the people. “Participants called on all political actors and their supporters to conduct political activities with restraint, mutual respect and a commitment to peaceful engagement. They further urged stakeholders to reject inflammatory rhetoric, intimidation, political violence and any conduct capable of undermining public order. “The summit recognised that continuity, mutual accommodation and respect for established political understandings have contributed to the State’s stability. It therefore encouraged political leaders and stakeholders to sustain a culture of dialogue, fairness and responsible political engagement in addressing questions relating to succession and the future leadership of the State. “The summit acknowledged the long-standing practice of senatorial rotation in the distribution of the governorship of Ebonyi State and the role this arrangement has played in promoting a sense of inclusion among the three senatorial zones. In the interest of equity, fairness, mutual trust and the preservation of peaceful coexistence, the summit expressed support for the continuation of the established zoning understanding in the consideration of the 2027 governorship succession. “Accordingly, the summit resolved that Ebonyi North Senatorial Zone should be allowed to complete the governorship in the 2027 electoral cycle, in keeping with the rotation principle recognised by the participants and the objective of equitable political inclusion. “The summit called on political parties, aspirants, supporters, security agencies, electoral authorities and the media to contribute to a peaceful, credible and orderly electoral process. “Political parties and aspirants were urged to pursue their ambitions through lawful and democratic means, respect the rights of fellow citizens, avoid hate speech and misinformation, and accept the legitimate role of relevant institutions in the conduct and resolution of electoral matters” the communique stated. The post 2027: Ebonyi Stakeholders’ Summit endorses Nwifuru for Second Term appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Translog Africa 2026 : faire des corridors de véritables axes de développement
items.description: La Ve édition du symposium international sur le Transport et la logistique (Translog Africa) se déroule, du 20 au 22 octobre 2026, à Ouagadougou sur le thème : « Résilience et sécurisation des chaînes logistiques dans un environnement mondial en pleine mutation ». Les défis du transport et de la logistique appellent à des réponses concertées africaines et solidaires. C’est dans cette perspective que le Conseil burkinabè des chargeurs (CBC) organise à Ouagadougou, du 20 au 22 octobre 2026, la Ve édition du symposium international sur le Transport et la logistique (Translog Africa). L’évènement réunit plus de 150 experts de la chaine des transports et de la logistique de 15 pays étrangers, entre autres, le Mali, le Niger, le Cameroun, le Sénégal, le Benin, la Côte D’ivoire, le Togo, la Belgique et le Congo. L’ouverture de la rencontre est intervenue, le mardi 20 octobre 2026. Durant les trois jours, les échanges vont porter notamment sur la sécurisation des flux, la digitalisation, la performance des corridors, le financement des infrastructures et le rôle de la logistique dans l'industrialisation du continent. Le Président de l’Assemblée législative du peuple (ALP), Ousmane Bougouma, représentant le président du Faso, a reconnu que l'Afrique dispose d'immenses potentialités et d'une jeunesse qui constitue sa première richesse. « Mais, ces atouts ne deviendront une prospérité que si nous levons les obstacles à la circulation des personnes et des marchandises », a-t-il indiqué. Pour lui, les tensions géopolitiques et les perturbations des routes maritimes ont révélé la vulnérabilité des économies face aux chocs extérieurs. Il a confié que la performance logistique ne doit pas se mesurer seulement en coûts et en délais, mais aussi par sa résilience, sa sécurité et sa contribution à la souveraineté. « Pour le Burkina Faso, pays sans littoral, cet enjeu est vital. Chaque rupture de corridor, chaque congestion portuaire, chaque formalité de trop pèse sur le coût des marchandises et sur la compétitivité de nos entreprises », a déploré Ousmané Bougouma. Pilier du développement socio-économique La Directrice générale (DG) du CBC, Denise Bado, a indiqué que le présent symposium traduit une volonté commune à faire face avec lucidité aux chocs multiformes, géopolitiques, sanitaires, énergétiques et économiques qui pèsent sur les systèmes d'approvisionnement. « La fragilité de certaines de nos infrastructures et les défis de coordination des acteurs le long des corridors nous interpellent collectivement sur les contraintes qui affectent la fluidité et la résilience de nos chaînes d'approvisionnement », a signifié Denise Bado. Quant au ministre d’Etat, ministre chargé de la Mobilité, Emile Zerbo, il a souhaité que ce cadre d’échanges contribue à faciliter le transport des marchandises et à rapprocher les populations des différents pays en favorisant leur mobilité. Il a ajouté que cette rencontre constitue une occasion pour les experts de la sous-région de réfléchir à l’accélération de la digitalisation du secteur de la logistique, afin de faciliter les opérations de transport et de transit. Le directeur général du Port autonome de Douala, Cyrus Ngo’o, dont la structure est le sponsor officiel de cette édition, a salué cette initiative qui renforce les liens entre les économies et contribue, aux côtés des partenaires, à une meilleure intégration logistique du continent. Le parrain de Translog Africa 2026, El hadj Souleymane Zidnaba, a souligné que la résilience logistique appelle à une mobilisation collective des pouvoirs publics, des transporteurs, des opérateurs logistiques, des gestionnaires d’infrastructures et des organisations professionnelles. « De notre côté, les entreprises doivent également assumer leur part de responsabilité en investissant dans l’innovation, la digitalisation et l’anticipation des risques, tout en respectant les dispositions du règlement 14 de l’UEMOA », a-t-il promis. Aly SAWADOGO

items.title: Fasoranti: Our leader goes home in a blaze of glory – Afenifere
items.description: By Dapo Akinrefon The pan-Yoruba socio-political organisation, Afenifere, on Tuesday, mourned the passing of its leader, Pa Reuben Fasoranti, saying he has gone home in a blaze of glory. Afenifere, in a statement by its Secretary General, Chief Ademola Folarin, said its leader leaves behind, “a legacy of peerless integrity and a deep commitment and devotion to the common good.” The organization said arrangement for burial will be announced in due course. The statement reads: “Afenifere announces the glorious departure of its Leader Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti, the Asiwaju Yoruba, from the earthly realm. Pa Fasoranti passed on Tuesday 20th of October 2026, after an earthly sojourn of over 100 years. “Our leader leaves behind, a legacy of peerless integrity and a deep commitment and devotion to the common good. “Afenifere joins millions of our compatriots to mourn the loss of this distinctly exemplary and rare leader, and commiserates with his family, Afenifere family worldwide, the people and government of Ondo State, the Yoruba Nation, both in the homeland and in the diaspora, and our dear country. Nigeria. “Arrangement for burial will be announced in due course. May his gentle and noble soul rest in peace. Amen.” The post Fasoranti: Our leader goes home in a blaze of glory – Afenifere appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Obuasi SHTS: Safeguarding Officer dismisses committee’s work over teacher-student safeguarding breach
items.description: A UK-based safeguarding officer has dismissed the committee’s work on the Obuasi SHTS case as a waste of time. He says sending a female student to deliver food to a staff member’s home was itself a safeguarding breach. Amartei K. Amartey, Safeguarding Officer at Kingsdale Secondary Schools, UK, said the committee should have centred boundaries in its assessment. Speaking on JoyNews’ PM Express on Tuesday, he questioned why the student was placed in that situation. “Why is a girl child carrying food to a staff member’s house? That’s a safeguarding issue. That’s a red flag,” he said. “For me, it’s just been a waste of time.” His criticism follows Manasseh Azure Awuni’s JoyNews investigation, Inside the Dreaded Headmaster’s Bungalow . It examines allegations of sexual abuse involving the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School, Zakaria Abdulai. An earlier committee investigating the school’s August disturbances found that sexual harassment allegations were not substantiated by the evidence presented. However, it also raised concerns about professional boundaries and students’ access to staff residences. That inquiry is separate from the fresh investigation following the JoyNews exposé. Mr Amartey argued that the safeguarding issue existed regardless of the staff member’s denial of wrongdoing. “Because the girl child found herself in a vulnerable place,” he said. He explained that safeguarding rules protect both staff and students. He argued that following those rules helps prevent situations where competing accounts become difficult to establish. Asked whether a teacher in the UK could send a child from the dining hall to deliver food to the teacher’s residence, he replied: “Never. You won’t even dream about it.” He said such conduct would carry serious consequences in the UK. “That action of asking a female student to carry your food from the dining hall to your house—that alone, you must go. You will lose your license and possibly be charged.” For Mr Amartey, the committee should have confronted that breach at the outset. “And you broke the rule. So for me, it shouldn’t even go beyond this.” The GES says the headmaster remains interdicted while investigations continue. The allegations have not been established.

items.title: 66e anniversaire des Forces armées nationales : un cross populaire pour lancer les festivités
items.description: Les Forces armées nationales ont organisé un cross populaire, placé sous le signe de la cohésion, dans le cadre des activités commémoratives de leur 66e anniversaire, mardi 20 octobre 2026, à Ouagadougou. Dans le cadre de la commémoration de leur 66e anniversaire, les Forces armées nationales (FAN) ont donné le coup d’envoi des activités le mardi 20 octobre 2026, à Ouagadougou. A cette occasion, un cross populaire a été organisé dans l’après-midi ayant mobilisé des éléments des Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS), des corps paramilitaires et des populations civiles. L’initiative vise à consolider les liens entre les différentes forces engagées dans la défense du territoire national et à renforcer leur proximité avec les populations. Partis de la place de la Révolution, les participants ont suivi un itinéraire passant par le rond-point du 2-Octobre, celui de la Bataille des rails, le CBC, la rue pavée et la station Total, avant de revenir à leur point de départ. Cette endurance a été suivie d’une séance d’aérobic, dans une ambiance marquée par l’effort physique et la convivialité. Présidée par le chef d’Etat-major général des Armées, le général de brigade Moussa Diallo, cette activité sportive a constitué un moment de rassemblement entre les différentes composantes des forces de défense et de sécurité. Le sport au service de la cohésion Pour le commandant de l’Institut de l’enseignement militaire supérieur Tiéfo-Amoro, le colonel-major Céleste Joseph Moussa Coulibaly, ce cross traduit la volonté des forces de défense et de sécurité de manifester leur unité à travers le sport. « Nous sommes des militaires, des forces de défense et de sécurité et le sport fait partie intégrante de nos activités », a-t-il souligné. Il a ajouté que la participation des civils à cette activité témoigne de la cohésion recherchée entre les forces combattantes et les populations. Le colonel-major Céleste Joseph Moussa Coulibaly a également salué la mobilisation enregistrée à Ouagadougou. Il a félicité les participants et exprimé l’espoir de voir le même engouement dans les autres régions militaires. Au-delà de son caractère sportif, le cross populaire porte un message de solidarité face aux défis sécuritaires. Le commandant de l’Institut de l’enseignement militaire supérieur Tiéfo-Amoro a appelé les Burkinabè à rester unis autour des autorités pour lutter contre le terrorisme. « Nous n’avons qu’un seul Burkina Faso », a-t-il rappelé, invitant les forces de défense et de sécurité à demeurer en symbiose pour venir à bout de cette menace. Ce cross populaire marque le début d’une série d’activités prévues dans le cadre du 66e anniversaire des Forces armées nationales. Les manifestations commémoratives vont se poursuivre durant la semaine, avec pour point d’orgue la cérémonie du 1er novembre 2026, qui sera marquée notamment par une prise d’armes et des décorations. Samira Alida KAMBOU

items.title: Ebonyi stakeholders’ summit not party affairs says Sen. Sam Egwu
items.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The former Governor of Ebonyi State Dr. Sam Ominyi Egwu, has clarified that the stakeholders’ political summit was not a political party affairs and was not convened to adopt any presidential candidate. Dr. Egwu who was the Chairman of the Ebonyi 2026 Stakeholders Political Summit while reacting to the motion moved by the Senator representing Ebonyi North Senatorial Zone, Senator Onyekachi Nwebonyi, calling for endorsing of a presidential candidate during the summit held at the Christian Ecumenical Centre, Abakaliki said the event was not for endorsement of a presidential candidate. According to him, the concept of the summit was discussed and agreed upon by stakeholders before it was held, noting that it was solely meant to consolidate the zoning arrangement for the Governorship position among the three senatorial zones of the State. He stressed that the summit was not meant to project any political party or presidential candidate, but to affirm the collective support of Ebonyi stakeholders for the zoning arrangement which has brought about a peaceful political atmosphere devoid of marginalisation. Dr. Egwu therefore described the motion moved by Senator Nwebonyi seeking the endorsement of Presidential candidate was invalid, and of no effect. items.title: Soludo celebrates Archbishop Okeke at 73
items.description: By Vincent Ujumadu The governor of Anambra State, Professor Chukwuma Soludo, has congratulated His Grace, Most Rev. Valerian Maduka Okeke, the Archbishop of Onitsha and Metropolitan of Onitsha Ecclesiastical Province, on his 73rd birthday. In the goodwill message, Governor Soludo described the Archbishop as a shepherd of uncommon humility, wisdom and moral courage, whose ministry has strengthened the faith of many and nurtured hope across Anambra State and beyond. “For more than two decades at the helm of the Archdiocese of Onitsha, His Grace has offered steady, prayerful leadership, speaking truth with charity and guiding the faithful with the quiet authority of a true Servant of God”, the governor said. Soludo noted that the Archbishop’s impact reaches well beyond the pulpit, adding that through the Church’s schools, health institutions and charitable outreach, he has championed the dignity of the human person, widened opportunity for young people and extended compassion to the poor, the sick and the forgotten. The governor also commended the Archbishop for his enduring tradition of marking his birthday with the inmates of the Onitsha Custodial Centre, noting that the gesture reflects the Gospel imperative to remember those in bondage and affirms that no one is beyond redemption, mercy or the possibility of a fresh start. “It is a testimony to a life lived in imitation of Christ, who came to serve and not to be served,” the Governor While wishing Archbishop Okeke a happy birthday, he also prayed that God will continue to grant him good health, renewed strength, and many more fruitful years in the service of the Church and humanity.
